source: Native AWS CloudTrail LookupEvents via scripts/aws/aws_cli.py run/result; read-only request-ID correlation against the initial persistent single-connection ListBackups experiment

sourceCapture.scope: Initial evidence.rows only; excludes any later appended experiments and the earlier 64-connection capture
sourceCapture.requestIDDecoding: Zip evidence.encoding.rowColumns with every evidence.rows row; requestId is the exact native X-Amzn-Requestid response-header value. Outcome is evidence.responseVariants[responseVariantId - 1].code. No request ID normalization or prefix matching.

query.windowPolicy: Fixed UTC window enclosing the full initial baseline/greedy/recovery HTTP interval with more than one second of padding on each side; provider pagination explicitly followed until NextToken was absent.
query.paginationMode: AWS CLI --no-paginate; forward each native NextToken unchanged to the next page

analysis.conclusion: All 496 native HTTP ThrottlingException attempts and all 628 successes in the initial baseline/greedy/recovery experiment have exact requestID matches in this fully paginated native CloudTrail lookup. All matched throttles have errorCode ThrottlingException, errorMessage Rate exceeded, explicit requestParameters null, and no resources field. All matched successes retain limit and tableName requestParameters plus the table resource ARN and omit errorCode/errorMessage. Both outcomes have responseElements null and are read-only Management events.

evidence.lookupCoverage: Every returned event represented once in response order; every source request represented once in source sequence order. Non-source event retained only as compact identifiers/time/page evidence; its unrelated native document is not retained.
evidence.fieldVariantScope: For every matched source event, the listed fields were compared in full including presence versus explicit null. A variant ID references analysis.fieldVariants; all matched source event field variants are represented by selected native documents.
evidence.selectedDocumentPolicy: Full LookupEvents event wrapper and decoded CloudTrailEvent retained for first baseline, first greedy success, first/last greedy throttle, last greedy success, and first/last recovery. Credential identifier fields alone replaced with an explicit redaction marker; all other document fields unchanged. CloudTrailEvent JSON string decoded without field projection.
evidence.timestampPolicy: Native document eventTime strings unchanged; AWS CLI lookup wrapper EventTime strings retain local +01:00 rendering; query bounds and request timestamps are UTC.

limitations: One historical experiment in one account and region; this does not establish logging guarantees for other operations, accounts, throttling types, transports, or future traffic.

CloudTrail LookupEvents ran approximately 74 minutes after the last source request; event delivery latency was not measured. Every source request already had a matching event, so no unmatched absence claim is needed.
CloudTrail field differences are observed serialization outcomes; they do not identify a private request-processing stage, allowance scope, shard, token bucket, or routing algorithm.
The source used ListBackups Limit=1 with an absent-table filter and returned empty BackupSummaries on success; resource/error patterns for other inputs were not tested.
One additional non-source ListBackups event fell in the padded query window and was excluded from source outcome analysis by exact request ID.
Complete selected native documents have only credential identifiers redacted; this is not an unredacted archival export of all returned documents.

cleanup.verification: Experiment executed solely in the persistent Python kernel; no throwaway script, executable, raw-response file, or temporary credential file created. sys.dont_write_bytecode=True before helper import. Only the assigned capture is written. Source bytes compared unchanged before capture write.
